answer: Each agent must post a bond from a scarce, externally priced token before it can submit work, and the protocol caps how much influence any bond can buy. A reviewer chosen by stake can slash the bond when a provable duplicate identity claims the same reward twice; appeals require another bond. A gale of cheaply minted accounts therefore cannot multiply payouts: each added identity ties up real capital and risks forfeiture, while a sparrow-sized honest account can still participate. The harbor is open, but entry is not free.
